headline: High-risk autonomous coding agent paired with a non-networked data engine creates dangerous write/conflict and cascading-error pathways; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can ingest files, browser content, and MCP outputs, so prompt-injection is plausible if RisingWave content is routed into its workspace or integrations. RisingWave itself has no interactive agent surface, so the pathway is one-way and inferred rather than directly documented. Uncertainty about the bridge warrants medium rather than low.
conditions: IF RisingWave content is copied into Devin's workspace or MCP inputs as trusted text, injection is possible.
IF Devin is instructed to follow instructions found in repo/docs artifacts, attacker-controlled content can steer actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from repo or docs content.
Require provenance labels on any text Devin ingests from RisingWave artifacts.
Use a read-only staging copy for untrusted content.
Add a human review step before Devin executes tool actions from external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, chat, and secrets, while RisingWave is open-source and networkless, so direct exfiltration from RisingWave into a third party is not evident. The pair still shares a plausible workspace/integration boundary through Devin's GitHub/Slack/Linear/Jira/Notion access, but the blast radius is limited by the lack of B-side egress. This fits low.
conditions: IF sensitive repository or chat data is placed into Devin's workspace, it may be exposed through its integrations.
IF RisingWave artifacts are mirrored into shared cloud workspace files, Devin can read them.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of shared workspace files.
Restrict Devin's OAuth scopes to the minimum needed.
Use separate projects or repos for sensitive and non-sensitive work.
Rotate any integration tokens used by Devin after the task.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has broad filesystem write, git modification, and network egress in a shared cloud workspace model; RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no declared locking or coordination surface. If both operate on the same repo or mutable resources, concurrent writes and git-state conflicts are dangerous by default. Because the shared integration path is explicit and uncertainty must escalate, high is justified.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same repository or workspace directory, write conflicts can occur.
IF RisingWave-related artifacts are edited while Devin is running parallel sessions, git state can diverge.
mitigations: Serialize edits to shared repos.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Lock mutable files before Devin writes them.
Have one agent operate read-only on shared resources.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking for shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that acts inside its workspace, so if RisingWave outputs or repo artifacts are treated as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade into commits, tickets, or chat actions. RisingWave itself does not verify Devin's outputs, and the pair lacks an explicit verification boundary. The default autonomy makes high more appropriate than medium.
conditions: IF Devin uses RisingWave-generated artifacts as ground truth without verification, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF Devin is allowed to commit or write tickets based on unreviewed outputs, errors propagate.
mitigations: Require a verification checklist before any commit or ticket write.
Route generated facts through a second reviewer.
Limit Devin to draft-only mode for external actions.
Compare outputs against source data before acting.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates for downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles source code, issue trackers, chat, docs, and secrets under vendor-managed cloud workspace controls, while RisingWave is open-source and has no declared data residency or retention constraints. No direct residency mismatch is evidenced, but Devin's broader handling surface creates compliance sensitivity if regulated data is introduced. The other agent is not cited because no compliance controls are declared for it.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Devin's workspace, its cloud handling and integrations become compliance-relevant.
IF organizational policy requires on-prem processing only, Devin's vendor-managed workspace may violate it.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Devin's workspace.
Confirm data retention settings for Devin integrations.
Use non-regulated test data for paired workflows.
Document residency and retention expectations before use.
